newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire defence official denies rebel takeover.
newsitem.headline: Zaire defence official denies rebel takeover.

text.p: Zairean rebels have taken the town of Kasenga, bringing them within 220 km (135 miles) of the country's second city, the copper capital Lubumbashi, expatriate and local sources said on Friday.
A Defence Ministry official in Kinshasa denied Kasenga had fallen.
"It is definitely rebel troops who are in control of Kasenga," said one source in Lubumbashi with contacts in Kasenga, a town of 17,000 south of Lake Mweru, on the river border with Zambia.
The expatriates, who declined to be identified, said Zairean soldiers retreated south and the rebels were in full control by midday.
They said injured civilians went to Kasenga hospital on Friday, seeking treatment after incidents with government troops.
But in the capital Kinshasa a Defence Ministry official denied Kasenga was the latest town captured by Laurent Kabila's rebels, who control about a quarter of the vast country.
"It is not true that Kasenga has fallen. Our troops are controlling the situation there perfectly. Whether it will fall in the next few days or not I cannot tell," he told Reuters.
A well-connected Lubumbashi businessman said Zairean military sources had confirmed the town's fall to him privately.
Kasenga is a small town with an airstrip and little else. It supplies Lubumbashi residents with their fish, caught in Lake Mweru.
The road from Lubumbashi to Kasenga is in poor condition, like most of Zaire's network, and what should be a two-hour journey takes eight. It has no functioning telecommunications.
